# `silk/platform/windows/time`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Exact conversions between Windows clock units and Silk instants.

## When to use
Windows providers use [`WindowsTime`](#WindowsTime) to convert FILETIME values, performance-counter ticks,
and blocking-wait durations. The conversions make no host calls and work on every target.

Import as `WindowsTime` with `import silk.platform.windows.time { WindowsTime }`.

Public declarations: 1.

<a id="WindowsTime"></a>

## `WindowsTime`

```silk
pub struct WindowsTime
```

Windows timestamp and timeout conversions without allocation or host calls.

### Details

FILETIME is unsigned 100-nanosecond intervals since 1601. Performance-counter values have a
nonnegative provider-local origin and a positive frequency. Invalid counter values trap.

## Implementation `WindowsTime`

```silk
impl WindowsTime
```

<a id="WindowsTime.impl.fileTime"></a>

### Associated function `fileTime`

```silk
pub fn fileTime(intervals: u64) -> Instant
```

Converts unsigned 100-nanosecond intervals since 1601 to Unix time.

#### Details

Every `u64` input is representable. Division precedes epoch subtraction and multiplication,
preserving dates before 1970 and avoiding overflow from a total nanosecond timestamp.

<a id="WindowsTime.impl.counter"></a>

### Associated function `counter`

```silk
pub fn counter(ticks: i64, frequency: i64) -> Instant
```

Converts nonnegative performance-counter ticks at `frequency` ticks per second to an instant.

#### Details

Fractional nanoseconds round down. Seconds and the fraction are converted separately, so
the total need not fit a nanosecond counter. Negative ticks or nonpositive frequency trap.

<a id="WindowsTime.impl.counterResolution"></a>

### Associated function `counterResolution`

```silk
pub fn counterResolution(frequency: i64) -> u64
```

Returns one performance-counter tick in whole nanoseconds, rounded up to at least one.
Nonpositive frequency traps. This is nominal resolution, not measured accuracy.

<a id="WindowsTime.impl.sleepMilliseconds"></a>

### Associated function `sleepMilliseconds`

```silk
pub fn sleepMilliseconds(seconds: i64, nanoseconds: i64) -> u32
```

Converts a canonical nonnegative duration to a finite Windows sleep timeout in milliseconds.

#### Details

Rounds up and saturates at 4,294,967,294, below Windows' infinite-wait sentinel. Callers
recheck their original deadline after each sleep. Negative seconds or nanoseconds outside
0 through 999,999,999 trap.
